scenarios.title: The loop script reads the branch format from its arguments or falls back to sdlc/{name}
scenarios.notes: Inputs: no branchFormat, empty string, a prefixed format. Empty string must fall back. INTERNALS must export BRANCH_FORMAT as a string and branchName as a function.

scenarios.title: branchName substitutes the placeholder and lowercases the tail for {name:lower}
scenarios.notes: Inputs: plain, prefixed and lower formats; tails with uppercase, '$&', '$1', '$$', slash, unicode, empty tail; a format with no placeholder; a format with both placeholders. String.replace treats '$' patterns in the replacement, so a hostile tail must not alter the result.

scenarios.title: The loop script and branches.py name the verifier branch the same way
scenarios.notes: Run branches.py name --kind verify for sdlc/{name}, feature/PROJ-1-{name} and feature/PROJ-1-{name:lower} with several ids, rounds, profiles and parts. Compare with rt.I.branchName on the tail <id>-v<round>-<profile>-<part>. Include a profile name with uppercase and a hyphen (http-api).

scenarios.title: verifyPhase builds the profile-agent and collector branches through the format
scenarios.notes: Run verifyPhase with a custom format and with the default. Check the branch passed to each profile agent and to the collector. The script source must hold no template literal that starts with sdlc/ followed by a substitution.

scenarios.title: The env-detector receives branchFormat
scenarios.notes: Inputs: no argument (null), an empty string (null), a format string. The input object must equal the five-key shape and carry the string unchanged.

tools.purpose: Generate tails and formats and call the loop functions
Run branches.py name from a scratch project and compare with the loop output
Hostile tails: dollar patterns, traversal, unicode, control characters

riskReason: The loop script names verifier branches, and a mismatch with branches.py breaks verification plumbing.
notes: No I/O boundary except the branches.py comparison. Contract is tagged first because it covers every scenario.
